newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends shade lower in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends shade lower in quiet trade.

text.p: * Central Bank firm in desired trading range
The Philippine peso ended a tad lower at 26.341 on Thursday from 26.240 as it was nudged down by corporate demand for the dollar, traders said.
In early trades, the peso had strenghtened to a high of 26.335 as one big bank sold the dollar after the U.S. Federal Reserve kept interest rates steady, a dealer said.
Later, corporate dollar demand and a $27-million requirement of oil companies capped the peso's strength, dealers said.
"The market was just sideways," a foreign bank dealer said.
Inflows were light due to the Chinese New Year Holidays, he said.
Moroever, the Central Bank kept its bid and offer rate for the dollar at 26.295/26.345, resulting in the peso being stuck in a tight band, they said.
The day's average was unchanged at 26.339, with volume rising to $136 million from $118 million.
